philosophy.summary: Grade desktop applications transparently against verifiable engineering controls. Binary supply-chain items state the exact requirement; architectural and vulnerability controls state what is graded and what needs to be fixed without prescriptive step-by-step fix recipes.

guidancePolicy.binary: Concrete yes/no operational control (for example: code signing certificate, published checksums, build provenance, security.txt).
guidancePolicy.outcome: General security boundary or attack-vector control. Reports the graded property, risk surface, and broad security outcome required — never step-by-step implementation instructions.

domains.name: Binary Identity & Supply Chain
domains.description: Cryptographic proof of publisher identity, artifact integrity, build provenance, and dependency hygiene.

domains.name: Runtime Isolation & Sandboxing
domains.description: Process sandboxing, renderer isolation, binary hardening, and safe execution boundaries.

domains.name: Privileges, Installers & OS Boundaries
domains.description: Least-privilege execution, locked file-system ACLs, and hardened installer/service boundaries.

domains.name: Secrets, Data & Local Networking
domains.description: Secret storage hygiene, loopback-scoped local APIs, and strict TLS validation.

domains.name: Auto-Update Integrity
domains.description: Authenticated, integrity-verified update delivery with downgrade protection.

domains.name: Verification & Automated Testing
domains.description: Automated regression coverage and continuous CI security scanning.

aiEraWatchlist.title: Unsigned or Unknown-Publisher Installers
aiEraWatchlist.redFlag: SmartScreen or Gatekeeper warns 'Unknown publisher', or the installer has no valid timestamped signature.
aiEraWatchlist.whyItMatters: AI makes convincing clone apps and trojanized installers trivial to generate; cryptographic code signing ties every byte to a verified publisher identity.

aiEraWatchlist.title: Silent Updates Without Integrity Checks
aiEraWatchlist.redFlag: The app downloads executables or scripts over plain HTTP or runs updates without verifying publisher signatures and checksums.
aiEraWatchlist.whyItMatters: A hijacked update channel turns a previously clean desktop app into an instant remote code execution vector.

aiEraWatchlist.title: World-Writable Directories Under Elevated Services
aiEraWatchlist.redFlag: A background service runs as SYSTEM/root while reading executables, configs, or secrets from folders any local user can modify.
aiEraWatchlist.whyItMatters: Standard-user write access to elevated service assets creates a direct local privilege escalation path.

aiEraWatchlist.title: Unauthenticated Local Servers Bound to All Interfaces
aiEraWatchlist.redFlag: A desktop helper binds to 0.0.0.0 or accepts cross-origin requests from any website in your browser.
aiEraWatchlist.whyItMatters: Malicious web pages or LAN devices can silently drive local desktop APIs if loopback binding and origin checks are missing.

aiEraWatchlist.title: Zero Transparency on Tests, Checksums, or Build Origin
aiEraWatchlist.redFlag: No published SHA-256 checksums, no build provenance, no security contact, and no evidence of automated security testing.
aiEraWatchlist.whyItMatters: In an era of AI-generated slopware, verifiable engineering receipts separate maintained software from opaque binaries.

controls.title: Code Signing & Trusted Timestamping
controls.gradedProperty: Distributable executables and installers are cryptographically signed with a trusted publisher certificate (such as Azure Artifact Signing, EV Authenticode, or Apple Developer ID + Notarization) with an RFC 3161 trusted timestamp.
controls.attackSurface: Unsigned binaries trigger OS trust warnings and cannot be distinguished from tampered or impersonated installers.
controls.whatToFix: Sign all release binaries and installers with a trusted code-signing certificate (e.g., Azure Artifact Signing / EV Authenticode on Windows, Apple Developer ID + Notarization on macOS) and include a trusted timestamp.

controls.title: Published Cryptographic Checksums
controls.gradedProperty: Every release publishes verifiable SHA-256 checksums (such as SHA256SUMS.txt or a signed release manifest with per-artifact hashes).
controls.attackSurface: Users and mirrors cannot independently verify that a downloaded installer matches the publisher's release output.
controls.whatToFix: Publish a deterministic SHA-256 checksum file (such as SHA256SUMS.txt) or manifest hashes alongside every release download.

controls.title: SLSA Build Provenance Attestations
controls.gradedProperty: Release pipelines emit signed build provenance attestations tying shipped binary digests to the exact source commit and CI workflow.
controls.attackSurface: Without build provenance, downstream users cannot verify that a signed binary was built from audited source rather than a compromised developer machine.
controls.whatToFix: Emit signed SLSA build provenance attestations from CI for release artifacts.

controls.title: Locked Dependencies & Vulnerability Scanning
controls.gradedProperty: Dependencies are pinned via committed lockfiles and scanned continuously for known CVEs.
controls.attackSurface: Unpinned dependency trees and unscanned packages expose desktop builds to supply-chain drift and known exploitable libraries.
controls.whatToFix: Commit deterministic dependency lockfiles and enable automated dependency vulnerability scanning in CI.

controls.title: Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
controls.gradedProperty: A clear security reporting channel is published (SECURITY.md and/or /.well-known/security.txt).
controls.attackSurface: Security researchers lack a safe, documented channel to report vulnerabilities responsibly.
controls.whatToFix: Publish a SECURITY.md policy in the repository and a /.well-known/security.txt contact on the project website.

controls.title: Electron Renderer Process Isolation
controls.gradedProperty: Browser windows enforce strict separation between web content and Node.js/OS privileges (context isolation enabled, Node integration disabled, OS sandboxing active).
controls.attackSurface: Exposed Node.js APIs or shared JavaScript contexts let any renderer script injection escalate straight into arbitrary OS command execution.
controls.whatToFix: Ensure all Electron renderers run with strict context isolation, no direct Node.js integration, and sandboxing enabled, exposing only minimal validated IPC bridges.

controls.title: Electron Web Security & Content Security Policy
controls.gradedProperty: Chromium web security remains enabled and a strict Content Security Policy constrains script execution, framing, and network origins.
controls.attackSurface: Disabled web security or permissive CSP removes browser-level origin isolation and makes cross-site scripting significantly more severe.
controls.whatToFix: Keep web security enforced across all windows and restrict script, object, frame, and network sources with a strict Content Security Policy.

controls.title: Electron Compile-Time Binary Fuses
controls.gradedProperty: Packaged Electron binaries disable dangerous runtime toggles (such as RunAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS, and CLI debugging flags) and restrict app loading to packaged archives.
controls.attackSurface: Default Electron binaries can be abused as a signed Node.js runtime or injected via environment variables to execute arbitrary code under a trusted signature.
controls.whatToFix: Harden packaged Electron binaries before signing so Node-runtime bypasses, environment-driven script injection, and unsigned external code loading are disabled.

controls.title: Tauri Capability Scoping & CSP
controls.gradedProperty: Tauri configuration defines a restrictive Content Security Policy and scopes filesystem, shell, and IPC capabilities to minimal required operations.
controls.attackSurface: Null CSP or overly broad shell/filesystem capabilities allow compromised webview content to read arbitrary files or execute OS commands.
controls.whatToFix: Enforce a non-null Content Security Policy and narrow Tauri capabilities so webviews cannot access unrestricted shell or filesystem scopes.

controls.title: Navigation, External URL & Command Execution Boundaries
controls.gradedProperty: External URL launches, navigation handlers, and OS process invocations validate schemes/inputs and avoid shell-interpolated execution of untrusted data.
controls.attackSurface: Unvalidated URL schemes (file://, smb://, custom handlers) or shell-expanded arguments enable command injection and local file execution.
controls.whatToFix: Restrict outbound URL launches and navigation targets to allowlisted schemes/origins, and eliminate shell-interpolated command invocation on untrusted inputs.

controls.title: Least-Privilege Execution & Directory ACL Hardening
controls.gradedProperty: Elevated services, installers, and shared application directories restrict write access strictly to administrative/service principals rather than standard users.
controls.attackSurface: World-writable config files, binaries, or service directories read by elevated processes create a direct local privilege escalation (LPE) and secret-exposure vector.
controls.whatToFix: Ensure elevated components and their configuration/binary directories deny write access to unprivileged local users, keeping user-writable data strictly separated from privileged paths.

controls.title: Installer & Bundled Service Boundary Hygiene
controls.gradedProperty: Installers avoid insecure binary search paths, unquoted service invocations, and overly permissive firewall or registry changes.
controls.attackSurface: Insecure installer scripting can introduce DLL hijacking, unquoted service path escalation, or lingering privileged footholds.
controls.whatToFix: Ensure installer definitions and service registrations quote executable paths, avoid broad permission grants, and cleanly tear down privileged components on uninstall.

controls.title: macOS Hardened Runtime & Minimal Entitlements
controls.gradedProperty: macOS builds enable Hardened Runtime and avoid dangerous entitlements such as disabled library validation or unsigned executable memory unless strictly justified.
controls.attackSurface: Relaxed macOS entitlements allow dylib injection and undermine Apple Notarization protections.
controls.whatToFix: Enable Hardened Runtime and remove unnecessary code-injection or unsigned-memory entitlements from the app bundle.

controls.title: Secret Storage & Hardcoded Credential Prevention
controls.gradedProperty: Source code and packaged bundles contain no hardcoded credentials, and runtime secrets rely on OS-backed encryption/keychain storage rather than plaintext files.
controls.attackSurface: Embedded tokens or plaintext local secret files can be extracted immediately by any local process or reverse engineer.
controls.whatToFix: Remove hardcoded secrets from source and build artifacts, and store sensitive local credentials using OS-protected secret storage.

controls.title: Loopback Binding & Local API Origin Enforcement
controls.gradedProperty: Local helper servers and IPC listeners bind strictly to loopback interfaces (127.0.0.1 / ::1) rather than 0.0.0.0 and enforce explicit origin/authentication checks.
controls.attackSurface: Local services bound to all interfaces or accepting wildcard CORS origins expose desktop control planes to LAN attackers and malicious web pages.
controls.whatToFix: Bind local-only services exclusively to loopback addresses and enforce strict origin and authentication checks on local API endpoints.

controls.title: Encrypted Transport & TLS Certificate Validation
controls.gradedProperty: Network communication uses encrypted transport (HTTPS/WSS) without disabling TLS certificate validation.
controls.attackSurface: Disabling TLS verification or transmitting sensitive data over plaintext HTTP exposes user sessions and payloads to network interception.
controls.whatToFix: Enforce HTTPS/WSS for all external endpoints and eliminate any code paths that disable TLS certificate verification in production.

controls.title: Authenticated & Integrity-Verified Auto-Updates
controls.gradedProperty: Auto-update mechanisms fetch metadata and binaries over HTTPS and cryptographically verify package signatures and digests before execution.
controls.attackSurface: Unverified update downloads allow man-in-the-middle or CDN compromise to execute arbitrary code on every user's machine.
controls.whatToFix: Ensure update delivery uses HTTPS and enforces cryptographic signature and hash verification before installing any update.

controls.title: Release Channel Separation & Anti-Downgrade Controls
controls.gradedProperty: Update publishing enforces monotonic version progression and isolates prerelease/beta tracks from stable production feeds.
controls.attackSurface: Missing version monotonicity or mixed channels allow rollback attacks to reintroduce previously patched vulnerabilities.
controls.whatToFix: Enforce monotonic version checks during release publication and isolate beta/prerelease feeds from stable production users.

controls.title: Automated Test Suite Coverage
controls.gradedProperty: The codebase maintains an automated test suite covering core functionality and security boundaries.
controls.attackSurface: Without automated tests, security boundaries and regression fixes silently degrade across releases.
controls.whatToFix: Establish and maintain automated tests covering critical application logic, input boundaries, and security-sensitive behaviors.

controls.title: Continuous CI Security Scanning
controls.gradedProperty: CI workflows automatically run static security analysis (SAST), secret scanning, and/or dependency auditing on pull requests.
controls.attackSurface: Vulnerabilities, leaked secrets, and vulnerable dependencies slip into releases unnoticed without automated PR gates.
controls.whatToFix: Add automated SAST (e.g., CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit), secret scanning (e.g., Gitleaks), and dependency CVE checks to CI pull request workflows.
